episode.title: Looking at the Sunni side of the aisle

persons.name: Sirajuddin Haqqani
persons.role: Head of the Haqqani Network; one of two Taliban deputy emirs; Taliban interior minister; US Specially Designated Global Terrorist; former $10M Rewards for Justice bounty (lifted 2025)
persons.status_detail: US lifted the $10 million reward for him in March 2025 in conjunction with the release of two American hostages

mentions.quote: the United States lifted the reward for one of our favorites, Sirajuddin Haqqani ... head of what is known as the Haqqani Network, a foreign terrorist organization. He himself has especially designated global terrorist. He had a $10 million reward
he's a deputy leader of the Taliban, but he's also al-Qaeda. And Al-Qaeda for decades

Sirajuddin Haqqani, who has the blood of thousands of Americans and Westerners on his hands ... that offensive that we watched as the Taliban took control of Afghanistan. He's the guy who put that together

when the Taliban played Weekend at Bernie's with Mullah Omar's corpse and issued statements and fatwas in his name ... Mullah Omar's brother and son started to walk away from the Taliban alliance. Siraj and his father, Jalaluddin, they put that band back together

persons.name: Jalaluddin Haqqani
persons.role: Founder of the Haqqani Network; father of Sirajuddin

mentions.quote: Siraj and his father, Jalaluddin, and they put that band back together

persons.name: Mullah Omar
persons.role: Taliban founder; death concealed while statements and fatwas were issued in his name
persons.status_detail: death concealed by Taliban leadership; disclosure led his brother and son to walk away from the alliance before the Haqqanis reunited it

mentions.quote: when the Taliban played Weekend at Bernie's with Mullah Omar's corpse and issued statements and fatwas in his name. And that was disclosed. And the Taliban's powerful factions, including Mullah Omar's brother and son started to walk away

persons.name: Ahmed al-Sharaa
persons.role: Leader of Hayat Tahrir al-Sham; now Syrian head of state
persons.status_detail: US lifted bounty on him and other HTS officials

mentions.quote: we also did that with Jolani and other HTS officials in Syria, now doing this again in Afghanistan
Jolani or Ahmed Shara, his real name, has to tow a fine line because he's now a world leader and has to have decent relations with Russia and by proxy China

persons.name: Hassan Mahsum
persons.role: Founder of the East Turkestan Islamic Party (late 1990s)

mentions.quote: That was the original name that its founder, Hassan Mahsum, used in the late 90s prior to going to Afghanistan

persons.name: Abdul Haq al-Turkistani
persons.role: Overall emir of the Turkestan Islamic Party (Afghanistan and Syria branches); member of al-Qaeda's main Shura since 2007

mentions.quote: It's overall Amir who leads both the Afghanistan branch and the Syria branch, Abdul Haq al-Turkistani is also an al-Qaida leader. He sits on al-Qaeda's main Shura
military leaders of the TIP in Syria that were appointed by Abdul Haq himself, an al-Qaeda leader

persons.name: Abu Khadija
persons.role: Islamic State deputy caliph (per CENTCOM); emir of the General Directorate of Provinces and of the Delegated Committee; formerly IS military emir and shadow governor of Diyala, then military commander for Iraq and Syria
persons.status_detail: killed in a US CENTCOM airstrike in Anbar province, Iraq (March 2025)

mentions.quote: We know him as Abu Khadija. He was killed by U.S. Central Command in an airstrike in Anbar province in Iraq ... CENTCOM described him as the deputy emir, possibly the deputy emir, the head of what is known as the general director of provinces ... the delegated committee
formerly the military emir of the Diyala province for the Islamic State. And then he rose up to being sort of the governor of Diyala ... then the overall military commander of Iraq and then Syria

persons.name: Abdul Qadir Mumin
persons.role: Leader of Islamic State Somalia; candidate (per US view) to be the Islamic State's overall caliph 'Abu Hafs'
persons.status_detail: survived a US strike attempting to kill him in May 2024; reportedly travels between Somalia and Yemen

mentions.quote: it was between Abu Khadija or Abdul Qadir Mumin in Somalia. And, you know, if Abdul Qadir wasn't Abu Hafs, then it was Abu Khadija and vice versa
Mumin's larger clan family, the Darod, which is one of the major Somali clans, they do claim lineage from Arabs
the U.S. did try to kill Mumin last May, but failed, but they haven't repeated that since

events.description: US lifted the $10 million Rewards for Justice bounty on Sirajuddin Haqqani in conjunction with the Taliban releasing two American hostages; talks between the US and Taliban ostensibly reopened.
Turkestan Islamic Party issued a new mission statement and reverted to its original name, East Turkestan Islamic Party, stressing Uyghur nationalism and omitting explicit Sharia language.
US CENTCOM airstrike in Anbar province killed Abu Khadija, described by CENTCOM as IS deputy emir and head of the General Directorate of Provinces and Delegated Committee.
US attempted to kill Abdul Qadir Mumin in Somalia but failed; Puntland counteroffensive against IS Somalia began afterwards.
US strike in Somalia killed an Omani Islamic State leader involved in external attack plotting.
US special operations raid in Somalia killed IS leader Bilal al-Sudani (hosts say 2023), a precedent for ground raids to seize intelligence.
Trump administration launched ~17 airstrikes in Somalia since February 2025 (vs 10 in all of 2024 under Biden; Trump 1 ~185, Biden total 48), after delegating strike authority to local commanders.
Shabaab attempted to assassinate Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud inside Mogadishu; mortars on the airport; checkpoints/IEDs on the outskirts.
Shabaab offensive reversing most federal-government gains of 2022-23; fighting in Lower and Middle Shabelle with fluid lines; Mogadishu sending prison guards and police to the front.
New York Times published a 'very kind' article calling Sirajuddin Haqqani a moderate just before the US election.
Abdul Haq al-Turkistani identified as a member of al-Qaeda since 2007.
Hassan Mahsum founded the group as the East Turkestan Islamic Party in the late 1990s before moving to Afghanistan, where it became TIP.

key_claims: Lifting the $10M reward on Sirajuddin Haqqani for two hostages legitimises the Taliban, invites more kidnappings, and delegitimises the designation/reward regime; Haqqani is 'also al-Qaeda' and architected the 2021 offensive.
Siraj and Jalaluddin Haqqani held the Taliban together after the concealed death of Mullah Omar was exposed and Omar's brother and son walked away.

TIP's rebrand to East Turkestan Islamic Party is window dressing: Abdul Haq al-Turkistani leads both branches, sits on al-Qaeda's Shura, and appointed the commanders now integrated into Syria's military; the Taliban's China ties force TIP to tread carefully.

Abu Khadija, killed in Anbar, was IS's general manager (GDP and Delegated Committee emir) and one of two caliph candidates; hosts doubt Abdul Qadir Mumin in Somalia is caliph for security, lineage and Iraqi-chauvinism reasons.
US should prioritise capture/exploitation raids against Mumin's node in Puntland and against ISKP, as done with Bilal al-Sudani.
Trump has delegated strike authority and sharply increased Somalia strikes (17 since Feb 2025 vs 10 in 2024), mostly against IS Somalia.
Shabaab is reversing 2022-23 government gains and probing Mogadishu, but claims of an imminent fall are 'bullshit'; watch for AU/US withdrawal signs.
